payload.structure: depth-3 ReLU cascade 3446->4739->2129 into hub 655, read out through 4 opposing-sign weights
payload.interpretation: stacked ReLUs with opposite-sign readout = piecewise-linear transfer curve with a few knots; flat for the ~90% with zero capital-gain, ramps for the minority with substantial gains

records.narrative: Closed-form expression for the capital-gain core, extracted symbolically through the DAG. The nested ReLU structure read out with opposing signs is the standard construction for a piecewise-linear threshold response. Because capital-gain is zero for the large majority of the population, the curve sits in a flat regime for most people and ramps the income score upward only for those with substantial gains. Analytical evidence (strongest form, tractable here).

payload.diagnosis: inert / excessive substructure - large weights (+1.10, -1.39) on tiny support = memorisation, not generalising signal
payload.description: Disable all five native-country one-hot edges fused into the capital-gain hub (-73->655, -81->655, -82->655, -89->2129, -94->2129), recompute on the full splits

records.narrative: Full-test-split re-run (supersedes the earlier subsample figures). The five native-country one-hots carry sizeable weights and structurally read as a country-conditioned distortion of the capital-gain threshold, yet disabling all five leaves performance unchanged to within 0.0001 AUC. Large weights on very few relevant rows indicate memorisation. Only holding structure and attribution together exposes this: structurally the terms look like signal, but ablation shows them inert on held-out data.

payload.why: The cascade's inner knots (z~-0.42, z~-0.03) fall below the data floor or are masked by the output hub's clipping; the four readouts (655/313/5102/6421) are all driven by capital-gain through the same hub, so they bend at one shared threshold - reshaping slope and offset but adding no further knots.
payload.caveat: bounded to the observed data range; the depth could act on out-of-distribution capital-gain values
payload.finding: Over the observed range of capital-gain the depth-3 cascade + 4-way opposing-sign readout collapses to a SINGLE-KNOT threshold: flat regime, one knot, then a linear ramp with constant slope across the entire data range (verified from the extracted partial-dependence curve, constant y-increment of ~0.246 per grid step after the knot). Functionally a single ReLU over the data.
payload.supersedes: the earlier analytical_formula record describing a 'piecewise-linear curve with a few knots'
payload.implication: depth exceeds the single threshold it produces over the data - excess structure, parallel to the inert native-country terms and the Heart 534 gate

records.narrative: CORRECTED analytical record (supersedes the earlier 'few knots' record). The capital-gain pathway is single-knot / single-ReLU-equivalent over the observed data range, not a multi-knot curve. Evidenced directly by the extracted transfer curve: constant slope after one knot, right to the maximum. The extra depth produces no additional knots within the data, making the depth itself a third instance of the paper's 'structure exceeds function' finding. Claim is bounded to the observed range.

payload.description: 53 of 107 one-hot input features are never connected by the evolved topology

records.narrative: Structural evidence, verifiable directly from the graph: these 53 inputs have no outgoing edges. Feature selection by omission is part of what full structural coverage makes explicit.

Whole-model performance and coverage summary. Complete structural and compositional coverage was reached with 9 identity-node insertions and ZERO function-changing operations: the explained network is computationally identical to the trained network. Small generalisation gap (0.0030 AUC).
